t: PDE: A different take on editing code

q.x: I've been using (neo)vim for years, and don't want to use anything else. It isn't just about productivity (I would probably be as productive in an IDE). It's because its _mine_. It's a highly customized environment, catered to my needs. [1] [link]

desc:
Today we talk about a new term that I'm coining called: PDE (Personalized Development Environment).

If you like this talk and/or style, please let me know in the comments. I would love to get your thoughts on branching out from just straight tutorial #neovim content and into something more general in #programming. 

Also, you might be interested in watching me on twitch if you enjoyed this talk,

recs.stt: Ask HN: Is Vim still worth learning?

recs.x:
I've been using (neo)vim for years, and don't want to use anything else. It isn't just about productivity (I would probably be as productive in an IDE). It's because its _mine_. It's a highly customized environment, catered to my needs.

[1] [link]

I've tried a lot of editors over the years... Currently I'm using neovim. It's been pretty nice--after some major adjustments. I like altering my configs and changing what's not working for me. Would I use it exclusively? No, but it's a nice tool to have in my toolbox. And with some effort it also can look very pretty.

[1]: [link]

recs.stt: Trying out Zed after more than a decade of Vim/Neovim
recs.x:
I will never understand how you go back from a very customized editor setup to the one with "reasonable defaults with little to no things to configure".
